title: A counterexample to Wall's D(2) problem
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's construction (2026) of a finite CW complex of dimension three that satisfies Wall's condition D(2) (no homology of the universal cover above degree two, no third cohomology with any coefficient module) and is not homotopy equivalent to a finite complex of dimension two. The new arguments are proved in full; six standard theorems of algebraic topology are used as named hypotheses with references to a free textbook. The first lesson states the problem, lists the standard theorems, and develops chain complexes twisted by a character of the fundamental group, with Fox derivatives for presentation complexes. The second lesson proves the tower obstruction: on a finite complex of dimension two, a character with vanishing twisted second homology is 1 on every element of finite order. The third lesson proves the finite plus construction and its cellular splitting. The fourth lesson gives the group with five generators and four relations, proves that the normal closure of two elements is perfect, computes the matrix of Fox derivatives at a character, and proves the theorem.
prerequisites: core course Algebraic Topology (D60): CW complexes, fundamental group, covering spaces, homology
groups, group rings and modules; tensor products over a ring
six standard theorems of algebraic topology are named hypotheses of the course (TOP1 to TOP6 in the first lesson); everything else is proved in the four lessons

checks.reading: The manuscript 'A Counterexample to Wall's D(2) Problem' (OpenAI, 6 Oct 2026, in the revision of the repository on 13 Oct 2026; four sections, one figure, about 700 lines of TeX) was read in full on 13 Oct 2026, and every step of its new arguments was derived again while the lessons were written: the rank argument over Laurent polynomials for infinite cyclic covers; the tower (Euler characteristic and the vanishing of H_0 give a map to Z; the lift exists because the first Betti number of the domain is zero; the vanishing of H_2 passes to the cover and to the image; the number of simplices of the image increases strictly and is bounded by that of the domain); the corollary on elements of finite order by the Moore complexes; the cellular splitting q d_3 = id of the plus construction and its three consequences; the two commutator identities, the two module equations and the coprime annihilators 26 and 15 for perfectness; the character; all twenty entries of the matrix of Fox derivatives; the minor -4 (1 - zeta^2). No error found. Differences of presentation, none a correction: the twisted chain complexes are defined by modules over the group ring and the cells of the universal cover throughout (the manuscript speaks of local systems); the lemma on cyclic covers is proved with the explicit ring homomorphism g -> rho(g) z^phi(g); the surjection onto the new cells in the plus construction is proved directly from H_1 = 0 of the intermediate cover, and the isomorphism of homology degree by degree, without the exact sequences of a pair; a finite simplicial model is taken from a textbook theorem instead of the manuscript's construction by mapping cylinders. Consistency checks beyond the manuscript: on the complex of dimension two with the two further cells for t_1 and t_2 (fundamental group G) the two new rows of the matrix are zero, so the twisted second homology has dimension two there, as the obstruction demands; applied to B itself the obstruction shows that x_1 has infinite order in P. Checked by the program plan/checks_20261013/d2_check.py (six parts: the character on the relators; the Fox derivatives by a program that differentiates the words, exactly in Q(zeta), against the matrix, with all five maximal minors; the zero rows for t_1 and t_2; the arithmetic of the perfectness proof; the general formula for relators x a x^-1 a^-n in 65 cases; the matrix over Laurent polynomials for the map s -> 1). It passed at the first run (output d2_check_run_20261013.txt). Statements of the standard theorems were located in the library copy of Hatcher's Algebraic Topology on 13 Oct 2026 (Propositions 1.26, 1.33, 1.39, Theorems 1.38, 2.35, 2.44, 2A.1, 2C.1, 2C.5, 4.32, Section 3.H, Example 2.42); their proofs were not checked. open_obligations: Named hypotheses TOP1 to TOP6 (first lesson): cells and the fundamental group; covering spaces of CW and simplicial complexes; cellular homology with the boundary of an attached cell and H_1 as the abelianized fundamental group; the Hurewicz theorem in degree two; homology and cohomology with coefficients in a module over the group ring, computed by the cells of the universal cover, with homotopy invariance and restriction to subcomplexes; simplicial approximation and finite simplicial models. They are standard textbook theorems, not proved in the programme in the form used. In the reference given (Hatcher), the statement that a covering of a CW complex is a CW complex with the lifted cells is an exercise, and the cellular form of homology with local coefficients is stated without a detailed proof. The theorem of the course is proved relative to these six hypotheses.

The core course Algebraic Topology (D60) covers part of TOP2 and TOP3; the exact locators in its texts have not been looked up. A foundation course on CW complexes, covering spaces and homology with coefficients in modules over the group ring would remove TOP1, TOP2, TOP3 and TOP5; TOP4 and TOP6 need lessons on the Hurewicz theorem and on simplicial approximation.

The statement that the finite D(2) problem goes back to Wall (1965) and is Problem D3 of a list of 1979 is taken from the manuscript; the sources were not read, and the literature was not searched for the current state of the problem.
The attaching maps of the two cells of dimension three are not explicit: they are given by the Hurewicz theorem.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
